posts.mainText: Sen. Warner's March 25 letter to OpenAI CEO Altman demands safeguards for military AI, urging coordination between DoD and firms to ensure ethical, lawful use amid rapid adoption.
posts.replyText: This event highlights legitimacy in AI governance: strong oversight builds public trust, coordinates stakeholders like DoD and companies, and upholds neutrality by rejecting unchecked "any lawful use" policies.

posts.mainText: Washington state enacted two AI laws on March 25: HB 2225 safeguards minors from companion chatbots; HB 1170 mandates disclosure of AI-generated content to users.
posts.replyText: State-level action demonstrates coordination through targeted protections, enhancing legitimacy by prioritizing vulnerable users like children, and neutrality via transparent AI deployment rules.

posts.mainText: White House published National Policy Framework for AI on March 25, outlining federal rules on child safety, IP, free speech, preempting burdensome state laws for unified governance.
posts.replyText: Federal framework fosters coordination across states, bolsters legitimacy via balanced protections and innovation, ensures neutrality by safeguarding free speech against ideological bias in AI.

posts.mainText: On March 26, White House and Sen. Blackburn unveiled visions for federal AI policy, including TRUMP AMERICA AI Act draft for uniform rules, child protections, and innovation sandboxes.
posts.replyText: Bipartisan push for federal AI policy promotes coordination to replace state patchwork, legitimacy through democratic protections like free speech, neutrality via industry standards over bureaucracy.

posts.mainText: Treasury announced conferences on March 25 to discuss reducing AI regulations for banks, convening experts to optimize oversight amid financial AI adoption.
posts.replyText: Initiative advances coordination in finance sector, legitimacy by tailoring regs to innovation needs, neutrality ensuring AI benefits economy without undue burdens on institutions.
